images.title: Both reduce to 3 : 2
images.purpose: Shows that 60 : 40 and 90 : 60 reduce to the same simplest form 3 : 2, so they are in proportion.
images.composition: Two rectangles side by side at the top, two arrows converging below them on one central box, and one line of notation at the bottom. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: Top left: a teal (#0072B2) rectangle 60 units wide and 40 units high with the label '60 : 40' under it. Top right: an amber (#E69F00) rectangle 90 units wide and 60 units high, drawn to the same scale, with the label '90 : 60' under it. A dark outline colour (#2B2B2B) arrow goes down from '60 : 40' to a central box, labelled '÷ 20'; a dark outline colour arrow goes down from '90 : 60' to the same box, labelled '÷ 30'. The central box is outlined in reddish purple (#CC79A7) and holds '3 : 2'. Under the box, the line '60 : 40 :: 90 : 60'. Exactly 2 rectangles, 2 arrows, 1 box.

images.takeaway: Two ratios with the same simplest form are in proportion.
images.description: Shows that 60 : 40 and 90 : 60 reduce to the same simplest form 3 : 2, so they are in proportion.
images.teaching_notes: Images A and D of the opening example; B (2 : 1) and E (1 : 1) are left out to keep one idea.

image_decisions.why: Reducing two different looking ratios to one simplest form is the step this concept teaches, and the converging arrows show it at a glance.
